title: BalancerPoolerV2.migrateMint emits no contract-level event; off-chain reconstruction must infer migration intent from the (ClaimBurned, N x ClaimMintedFor) byproduct pattern
severity_rationale: Low / QA. Pure observability gap with no runtime exploit. Off-chain accounting / indexers must perform a structural match against byproduct emissions to attribute 'this user migrated' vs 'this user burned id-4 elsewhere and an unrelated minter happened to mint id-6 to the same recipient.' The structural match works today because the pooler is the only authorized burner of id-4 and the only path that calls both burn and mintFor in one tx, but the invariant is implicit. Per C4: QA/Low — events / observability are explicitly QA-tier concerns.
description:
migrateMint emits no event of its own. The only on-chain trace is the byproduct emission from NFTMinterV2: one `ClaimBurned(holder=msg.sender, tokenId=4, quantity=amount)` plus `amount` separate `ClaimMintedFor(recipient=mintRecipient, dispatcherIndex=6, minter=address(this))` events. Off-chain indexers / accounting systems that need to distinguish 'this user migrated via migrateMint' from 'this user burned id-4 via some other authorized burner and an unrelated authorized minter happened to mint N id-6 to the same recipient' have to match: same tx hash, ClaimBurned.quantity == count of adjacent ClaimMintedFor with matching recipient + minter==pooler.

This also makes on-chain rate-limiting infeasible: any consumer contract that wants to react to 'a migration happened' must register either a ClaimBurned or ClaimMintedFor handler and pattern-match itself. A first-class `Migrated` event on the dispatcher would let downstream consumers subscribe directly.

The docstring describes the behaviour ('Burn `amount` of id-4 from msg.sender and mint `amount` of id-6 to mintRecipient'), but no event documents the (caller, mintRecipient, amount) tuple. Reorg-aware indexers ordinarily key off function-level events; here they have to special-case the emission pattern.
exploit_path:
Not a runtime exploit. The harm is observability:
1. An off-chain accounting system wants to compute 'how many id-4 holders have migrated, and how many id-6 NFTs are migration-origin vs paid-mint-origin.'
2. The only on-chain signals are ClaimBurned (tokenId=4) and ClaimMintedFor (dispatcherIndex=6). The indexer must structurally match the two.
3. If the protocol later authorises a second burner of id-4 (e.g., a separate redemption path) or a second minter of id-6 (e.g., a giveaway / promotional mint), the structural match breaks. The indexer silently mis-attributes. Off-chain rewards may pay the wrong cohort.
mainnet_realism_check: Pure observability gap. Mainnet indexers are aware of this class of issue and consistently flag missing first-class events as a maintainability concern.
recommendation: Add `event Migrated(address indexed caller, address indexed mintRecipient, uint256 amount, uint256 oldNftId, uint256 newNftIndex);` and emit it once at the end of migrateMint. This makes downstream consumers reorg-safe and structurally simple, future-proofs against additional authorized burners / minters, and makes the intent visible in explorer logs.
